item.title: Protests roil France once again as police seek to quell violence
item.description: Hundreds of thousands turned out across France to protest everything from the lack of school funding to economic inequality. Police also were out in force to prevent a repeat of last week's violence.

item.title: Why a far-right cabinet minister in Israel has Netanyahu's ear
item.description: Israel's most far-right cabinet minister helped dictate hardline policies toward Palestinians in recent years. Benjamin Netanyahu vows to give him a senior position if Netanyahu is reelected next week.

item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that normal Starlink operating speeds were restored after more than a week of disruptions.

item.title: Gunmen open fire at a church during a funeral in Jordan, killing 7 and wounding 40
item.description: Footage broadcast on Jordanian state television showed three gunmen firing shots at a Greek Orthodox church in the city of Karak on Friday.

item.title: European student protests take aim at Serbia's elections
item.description: Students have been protesting across Europe. In Serbia, they've selected candidates to run for parliament in Sunday's elections. And they're aiming to end 14 years of government by the populist leader Aleksandar Vucic.

item.title: Drinking water supplies dwindle in Yemeni city besieged by Houthi rebels
item.description: Taiz, a city in southwestern Yemen, faces a severe water crisis as Houthi rebels backed by Iran tighten their encirclement. The city has struggled with water issues for over a decade, but the situation has worsened in recent weeks.

item.title: Israeli PM pledges massive military operation after West Bank checkpoint attack
item.description: Israel's Prime Minister is vowing to launch a major military operation in the West Bank in response to an attack by two Palestinian gunmen on an Israeli military checkpoint that killed two soldiers.

item.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
item.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

item.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early

item.description: NPR'S Leila Fadel speaks with retired four-star Gen. Joseph Votel about the war in Iran and the U.S. and Israeli objectives for a potential post-election bombing campaign.
